To calculate the difference between simple and compound interest at 14% per annum on a sum of Rs. 1000 after 4 years:

**Simple Interest (SI):**
$$ \text{SI} = P \times r \times t $$
Where:
- $ P = 1000 $
- $ r = 14\% = 0.14 $
- $ t = 4 $

$$ \text{SI} = 1000 \times 0.14 \times 4 = 560 $$

**Compound Interest (CI):**
$$ \text{CI} = P \left(1 + r\right)^t - P $$
$$ \text{CI} = 1000 \left(1 + 0.14\right)^4 - 1000 $$
$$ \text{CI} = 1000 \left(1.14\right)^4 - 1000 $$

Calculate $ (1.14)^4 $:
$$ (1.14)^2 = 1.2996 $$
$$ (1.14)^4 = (1.2996)^2 \approx 1.68896 $$

$$ \text{CI} = 1000 \times 1.68896 - 1000 = 1688.96 - 1000 = 688.96 $$

**Difference:**
$$ \text{Difference} = \text{CI} - \text{SI} = 688.96 - 560 = 128.96 $$

Rounding to the nearest whole number, the difference is approximately **129**.
